issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines Pneumatic.openValve() with no parameters, but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration). The implementing classes in the solution (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement openValve() with no parameters, which contradicts the Pneumatic interface declaration and will cause a compilation/signature mismatch. This inconsistency between the problem UML, the solution interface, and the implementing classes will confuse students and block correct implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.openValve signature consistent with the UML/problem statement and the implementing classes. Change the interface declaration to void openValve(); (no parameters) in Pneumatic.java in both template and solution. Alternatively, if an int parameter is intended, update the UML/problem statement and update all implementing classes to declare openValve(int) accordingly. The recommended fix is to update Pneumatic to declare openValve() with no parameters so it matches the UML and the current implementations.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines Pneumatic.openValve() with no parameters (openValve(): void), but the provided solution declares Pneumatic.openValve(int duration). This creates a mismatch between the problem specification and the solution: the method name is the same but the signature differs (extra parameter). Students will be confused which signature to implement and this also conflicts with the concrete ride classes in the solution (which implement openValve() with no parameter).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.openValve method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's Pneumatic interface to declare openValve() with no parameters to match the UML/problem statement, and keep the implementing classes' openValve() methods parameterless; or (B) update the problem statement/UML and any guidance to specify openValve(int duration) and update all implementing classes and templates accordingly. Ensure all implementations and the interface use the exact same signature.
